sections.overview: The Great Evening Bat occurs from northeastern India and Nepal to southern China and mainland Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: It is among the largest vespertilionids, with grey-black dorsal fur, a browner underside and broad ears on a bare face.
sections.habitat: The species is associated with tropical moist forests and roosts in caves, including records from high-elevation sites.
sections.diet: It can prey on birds: DNA metabarcoding identified 22 passerine species in one study. Other field work also reported insects among its prey.
sections.behavior: Research documents both aerial attacks and gleaning as possible ways it takes small songbirds, but the study does not establish that every prey capture uses either method.
sections.reproduction: A historical Sichuan sample found 83% of females collected on 25 April pregnant, each with one embryo; this is a single dated sample, not a full breeding calendar.
sections.ecology: Unlike many bats, it eats birds and roosts in caves.
sections.conservation: IUCN assessed it as Near Threatened in 2018, citing forest loss and cave development.
